data.name: Senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)
data.description: Inflammatory secretory programme of senescent cells, supported translationally by mTORC1.
data.description_beginner: The inflammatory signals that senescent cells pump out.

studies.title: mTOR regulates the pro-tumorigenic senescence-associated secretory phenotype by promoting IL1A translation
studies.authors: Laberge RM; Sun Y; Orjalo AV; Patil CK; Freund A; et al.; Campisi J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Explained HOW rapamycin calms 'inflammaging'. Senescent cells spew inflammatory signals (the SASP) that damage surrounding tissue and even feed tumors. mTOR powers this by translating IL1A, the cytokine at the top of the cascade. Rapamycin selectively shuts it down - and blocked senescent cells from fueling prostate tumor growth in mice.

studies.title: Impaired Chaperone-Mediated Autophagy Accelerates Intervertebral Disc Degeneration by Inducing MIDN Accumulation to Target TSC2 for Proteasomal Degradation
studies.authors: Chen Xianglong; Gao H; Wu W; Shi P; Chen Yuhang; Zhang A; Cheng Z; Wu W; Yu Z; Zhang Y

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human nucleus pulposus cells; rat caudal needle-puncture model
studies.finding: Loss of chaperone-mediated autophagy lets its substrate midnolin (MIDN) accumulate; MIDN binds TSC2 and drives its proteasomal degradation independently of ubiquitination, de-repressing mTORC1 and causing senescence, SASP and matrix loss in disc cells. MIDN knockdown, LAMP2A overexpression or rapamycin each blocked the degeneration - a new upstream route to mTORC1 hyperactivation.

studies.title: Spatial coupling of mTOR and autophagy augments secretory phenotypes
studies.authors: Narita Masako; Young AR; Arakawa S; Samarajiwa SA; Nakashima T; Yoshida S; Hong S; Berry LS; Reichelt S; Ferreira M; Tavare S; Inoki K; Shimizu S; Narita Masashi

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human and mouse cells (Ras-induced senescent fibroblasts, macrophages, podocytes)
studies.finding: Protein synthesis and autophagic degradation are usually described as opposites that mTOR switches between, and this paper shows a compartment where the cell deliberately runs both at once. In senescent cells, autolysosomes and mTOR gather at one side of the Golgi (the TASCC), mTOR gets there in an amino-acid- and Rag-dependent way, and destroying that arrangement cuts interleukin-6/8 secretion. Boundary: cells, not organisms; it explains how the senescent secretory programme is fuelled, not whether blocking it helps an animal.

studies.title: Therapeutic reversal of cellular senescence: A systematic review of senolytics, senomorphics and anti-ageing therapies in human clinical trials
studies.authors: Trivedi H; Tripathi S; Thacker J; Patil N; Shaikh S

evidence.label: Synthesis of human data
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human clinical trials (PRISMA 2020 systematic review, 6 completed studies + 1 ongoing)
studies.finding: A PRISMA-guided systematic review of the only six completed human clinical trials testing drugs that clear or calm senescent ("zombie") cells -- senolytics such as dasatinib+quercetin, plus senomorphic and mTOR-targeting approaches -- found modest, biomarker-level improvements with mostly mild side effects, but judged the evidence too thin (small samples, short follow-up) to call any of it an established therapy yet. Useful mainly as a rare systematic look at where human senescence-targeting trials, mTOR inhibitors included, actually stand today -- not as proof that any one drug works.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 sustains the inflammatory secretory output of cells that are already senescent, by promoting IL1A translation. Inhibiting it quietens that output without reversing the proliferative arrest.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 keeps old, "senescent" cells pumping out inflammatory signals, and blocking it calms that output down without making those cells young again. Whether mTORC1 also helps push cells into senescence in the first place is a separate question this arrow does not answer.
relations.boundary: Three studies, all in cells or a rat disease model. LAB2015 and NAR2011 measure the secretory output of cells that are already senescent (IL1A translation; IL-6/IL-8 production fuelled by mTOR at the TASCC). CHEN2026C (human disc cells, rat needle-puncture model) shows mTORC1 hyperactivation after TSC2 loss together with senescence and SASP, both blocked by rapamycin - a disease-model result, not a general demonstration that mTORC1 drives cells into senescence. That is why this arrow lands on the secretory programme and not on senescence itself.
relations.note: The arrow means mTORC1 sustains the secretory output (SASP) of senescent cells. Whether mTORC1 also pushes cells into senescence in the first place (geroconversion) is a separate and weaker claim that this edge does not make.
